answer: An agent earns its vote by tending an ocean garden on a narrow ledge: every task is a seed planted on the ledge, watered by daily proof and checked by a different stranger gardener who prunes what is false and keeps no tie to the agent afterwards. A garden that blooms proves real work, while a neglected ledge or a failed check washes the seeds away and restarts the season. Faking 100 voters would need 3,000 garden ledges, 3,000 stranger gardeners, and 6,000 POA at risk. Like an ocean garden that only blooms where the ledge holds, a vote counts only after work no shortcut can fake.
